variants.title: Advance one latent
variants.context: In latent diffusion the model predicts an update and the scheduler applies it. Repeating that pair across the selected noise levels produces the final latent, which the decoder turns into pixels.
variants.prompt: A text-only job runs on a worker that already holds the pinned bundle. Put the denoising path in order.

items.text: At the current noise level, predict the target the checkpoint was trained to produce.
Create the initial latent tensor from the recorded seed and the requested shape.
After the final scheduled update, decode the latent and package the pixels for evaluation.
Let the scheduler use that prediction to compute the next latent.
Tokenize and encode the prompt, negative conditioning, and any control inputs under versioned preprocessing.

variants.hint: The model predicts; something else applies.
variants.explanation: The checkpoint owns the prediction target and the scheduler owns the numerical path between noise levels.

variants.title: Advance one latent
variants.context: In latent diffusion the model predicts an update and the scheduler applies it. Repeating that pair across the selected noise levels produces the final latent, which the decoder turns into pixels.
variants.prompt: The generation profile enables classifier-free guidance. Put the steps of the guided loop in order.

items.text: Evaluate the denoiser on both conditioning paths at the current noise level.
Encode both the prompt conditioning and the unconditional or negative conditioning for this request.
Repeat until the final scheduled noise level, then decode the latent.
Let the scheduler apply the combined prediction to reach the next latent.
Sample the starting latent from the recorded seed and the requested shape.
Combine the conditional and unconditional predictions using the guidance scale.

variants.hint: Guidance acts on predictions, before the scheduler sees them.
variants.explanation: Guidance combines two predictions into one update, so the second conditioning path costs compute while the scale itself does not add model calls.

variants.title: Advance one latent
variants.context: In latent diffusion the model predicts an update and the scheduler applies it. Repeating that pair across the selected noise levels produces the final latent, which the decoder turns into pixels.
variants.prompt: A prompt edit produced no visible change in the output. Put the stages an investigator checks in the order they run.

items.text: Check that the denoiser actually received the conditioning when it predicted its target.
Check that the scheduler applied those predictions rather than replaying a cached trajectory.
Check that the decoded pixels came from this job's final latent and not a stored asset.
Check that preprocessing and the text encoder version turned the edited prompt into different conditioning values.
Check that the recorded seed and shape produced the expected starting latent.

variants.hint: Walk the path forward and stop at the first stage where the change disappears.
variants.explanation: Conditioning can be lost at any boundary, so the manifest records preprocessing, encoder, seed, scheduler, and output digest to make that walk possible.

variants.title: Run the production request path
variants.context: The denoising loop is a GPU kernel workload but the product is a durable media job. The control plane admits work, the scheduler queues compatible work, a worker generates under a lease, policy evaluates before publication, and delivery commits one terminal result.
variants.prompt: A tenant submits a standard job through the API. Put the production stages in order.

items.text: Load the pinned bundle, claim a bounded lease, propagate cancellation, and emit progress.
Atomically record the terminal state and object reference, notify once, and retain the execution manifest.
Queue the job alongside requests sharing its model, shape, conditioning, precision, and safety contract.
Authenticate the tenant, normalize parameters, classify policy, estimate work, reserve quota, and assign an idempotent job ID.
Run output safety, quality, and provenance checks outside the model, failing closed when a mandatory decision is unavailable.

variants.hint: Which stage is the only one that can refuse the work cheaply?
variants.explanation: Admission, scheduling, generation, policy, and delivery are separate responsibilities so an incident can name where a job stopped.

variants.title: Run the production request path
variants.context: The denoising loop is a GPU kernel workload but the product is a durable media job. The control plane admits work, the scheduler queues compatible work, a worker generates under a lease, policy evaluates before publication, and delivery commits one terminal result.
variants.prompt: A worker stops heartbeating mid-job and the coordinator does not know whether anything was published. Put the recovery steps in order.

items.text: Reconcile whether an accepted output already committed for this job identity.
The lease expires because the worker stopped heartbeating.
Commit the output with a compare-and-set on job identity so two workers cannot publish two results.
Notify once and record the retry lineage in the execution manifest.
Retry only from that known state, charging the attempt to the original quota and deadline.

variants.hint: An unknown completion state is not a known state.
variants.explanation: Blind retries turn an ambiguous timeout into duplicate GPU work or duplicate publication, so reconciliation comes before another expensive attempt.

variants.title: Run the production request path
variants.context: The denoising loop is a GPU kernel workload but the product is a durable media job. The control plane admits work, the scheduler queues compatible work, a worker generates under a lease, policy evaluates before publication, and delivery commits one terminal result.
variants.prompt: The mandatory output detector is unavailable after a candidate is decoded. Put the steps in order.

items.text: The policy fails closed rather than silently bypassing the missing check.
The required output check reports that it cannot return a decision.
The manifest records the policy version, the unavailable check, and the terminal reason.
The worker finishes decoding and holds the candidate unpublished.
The job routes to review or to a bounded safe mode.

variants.hint: What is the safe default when required evidence is missing?
variants.explanation: Mandatory checks fail closed, and prompt admission and output publication stay separate controls with their own versions and thresholds.

variants.title: Count the model evaluations
variants.context: Each scheduled step buys denoiser evaluations. Classifier-free guidance evaluates a second conditioning path, so enabling it changes compute, while raising the guidance scale changes how the predictions combine without adding model calls.
variants.prompt: A profile runs 28 scheduled steps with classifier-free guidance enabled at a scale of 3.0. How many denoiser evaluations does the job spend?
variants.hint: Count the conditioning paths, then the steps.
variants.explanation: Guidance evaluates a conditional and an unconditional path at each scheduled step, so the second path doubles the model calls.

mistakes.feedback: You counted one evaluation per step and dropped the unconditional path.
You multiplied by the guidance scale, which changes the combination rather than the number of calls.

variants.title: Count the model evaluations
variants.context: Each scheduled step buys denoiser evaluations. Classifier-free guidance evaluates a second conditioning path, so enabling it changes compute, while raising the guidance scale changes how the predictions combine without adding model calls.
variants.prompt: A profile already runs 40 steps with classifier-free guidance enabled. An operator raises the guidance scale from 5.0 to 9.0 and leaves the step count alone. How many denoiser evaluations does the job now spend?
variants.hint: Ask which of the two settings buys model calls.
variants.explanation: Raising the guidance scale changes how the two predictions combine; only the step count and the number of conditioning paths change the call count.

mistakes.feedback: You multiplied steps by the new guidance scale, but the scale does not add model calls.
You dropped the second conditioning path that guidance requires.

variants.title: Count the model evaluations
variants.context: Each scheduled step buys denoiser evaluations. Classifier-free guidance evaluates a second conditioning path, so enabling it changes compute, while raising the guidance scale changes how the predictions combine without adding model calls.
variants.prompt: A team cuts a guided profile from 50 scheduled steps to 20, leaving classifier-free guidance enabled. How many denoiser evaluations does the change save?
variants.hint: Every removed step removes both conditioning paths.
variants.explanation: Sequential model evaluations are the dominant cost, so removing steps saves the removed steps times the number of conditioning paths.

mistakes.feedback: You subtracted the step counts without counting both conditioning paths.
That is the new evaluation count, not the number saved.

variants.title: Bound the serving path
variants.context: Batching, precision, queueing, retry, safety, and rollout settings are coupled. Named generation profiles with validated ranges keep arbitrary client parameters from buying unbounded work.
variants.prompt: A scheduled campaign export fills the shared queue and interactive previews start missing their deadline. What is the right fix?
options: Separate the interactive, standard, and offline queues and admit work against reserved GPU seconds.
Raise the batch size so the export drains faster and the previews resume sooner.
Add GPUs and keep one queue, since capacity is the only real constraint here.
optionFeedback: Correct: queue isolation plus admission against reserved GPU seconds keeps batch work out of interactive slots.
Wrong: a larger batch waits longer to fill and uses more memory, which hurts interactive latency further.
Wrong: one shared queue lets the next export consume the new capacity exactly as before.
variants.hint: A queue full of the wrong work is an admission problem.
variants.explanation: Preview, standard, and offline queues stay separate so one campaign export cannot consume every interactive slot.

variants.title: Bound the serving path
variants.context: Batching, precision, queueing, retry, safety, and rollout settings are coupled. Named generation profiles with validated ranges keep arbitrary client parameters from buying unbounded work.
variants.prompt: A benchmark on a developer workstation shows a lower precision mode halves memory and speeds up generation. What should the release do next?
options: Promote it everywhere, since precision affects memory rather than image content.
Reject it outright, since any precision change makes generated output unreliable.
Validate quality, speed, and numerical drift for that precision on the exact target stack.
optionFeedback: Wrong: precision changes outputs, which is why offline evidence includes drift across precision variants.
Wrong: lower precision is a supported optimization once its effect is measured on the target stack.
Correct: the exact quality and speed change has to be validated on the target model, kernels, and hardware.
variants.hint: Which stack produced that benchmark number?
variants.explanation: Lower precision can reduce memory and accelerate supported operations, but the quality and speed change must be measured on the deployment hardware and kernels.

variants.title: Bound the serving path
variants.context: Batching, precision, queueing, retry, safety, and rollout settings are coupled. Named generation profiles with validated ranges keep arbitrary client parameters from buying unbounded work.
variants.prompt: A client library passes any step count, resolution, and guidance value straight through to the worker. What should the service do?
options: Publish named generation profiles with validated ranges and reject or route work outside them.
Accept any value and rely on the worker timeout to bound the cost of extreme requests.
Cap only resolution, since memory is the binding limit and steps only affect quality.
optionFeedback: Correct: validated profiles keep client parameters from choosing unbounded sequential work.
Wrong: a timeout wastes the GPU seconds already spent and gives the caller no honest answer.
Wrong: step count buys sequential model evaluations, so it drives latency as directly as resolution.
variants.hint: Who is choosing how much GPU time the request buys?
variants.explanation: Publish named profiles with validated ranges, then reject or asynchronously route requests that exceed those envelopes.

variants.title: Assign the responsibility
variants.context: A diffusion service separates responsibilities: what the checkpoint, scheduler, step count, guidance, and seed each own, what each failure class requires, and what the execution manifest must record. Matching the part to its job is what makes a result explainable.
variants.prompt: An incident review argues about which setting caused a change. Match each part of the inference contract with what it owns.

pairs.label: Model checkpoint
pairs.detail: Defines what target is predicted and which conditioning and noise schedule it was trained for.

pairs.label: Scheduler
pairs.detail: Defines the numerical path between selected noise levels and is not a drop-in upgrade for every model.

pairs.label: Step count
pairs.detail: Selects how many model evaluations the request buys from that path.

pairs.label: Classifier-free guidance
pairs.detail: Combines conditional and unconditional predictions to trade prompt adherence against diversity.

pairs.label: Random seed
pairs.detail: Initializes the noise, while replay also depends on precision, kernels, and library versions.

variants.hint: One of these decides the path and one decides how much of the path you buy.
variants.explanation: Separating these five prevents a contract change from being misread as a model quality regression.

variants.title: Assign the responsibility
variants.context: A diffusion service separates responsibilities: what the checkpoint, scheduler, step count, guidance, and seed each own, what each failure class requires, and what the execution manifest must record. Matching the part to its job is what makes a result explainable.
variants.prompt: A readiness review lists four failure classes. Match each one with the control that is supposed to contain it.

pairs.label: Queue overload
pairs.detail: Shed, degrade, or defer before queue age exceeds the remaining user deadline.

pairs.label: Worker loss
pairs.detail: Lease for a bounded period and commit outputs with a compare-and-set on job identity.

pairs.label: Safety dependency failure
pairs.detail: Fail closed for mandatory checks and route to review instead of bypassing policy.

pairs.label: Model rollout regression
pairs.detail: Canary by stable traffic identity and roll back the versioned bundle as one unit.

variants.hint: Each failure has one control that stops it from becoming a second failure.
variants.explanation: Naming the control before launch is what turns each of these from an outage into a bounded, recorded outcome.

variants.title: Assign the responsibility
variants.context: A diffusion service separates responsibilities: what the checkpoint, scheduler, step count, guidance, and seed each own, what each failure class requires, and what the execution manifest must record. Matching the part to its job is what makes a result explainable.
variants.prompt: An investigator opens the execution manifest for one job. Match each recorded group with the question it answers.

pairs.label: Idempotency identifiers
pairs.detail: Whether a client retry bought a second generation.

pairs.label: Bundle versions
pairs.detail: Which model, encoder, autoencoder, scheduler, adapter, and policy produced the image.

pairs.label: Sampling fields
pairs.detail: Which seed, dimensions, step count, guidance, and precision were spent.

pairs.label: Stage timings
pairs.detail: Whether queue, load, denoise, decode, safety, or storage consumed the latency.

pairs.label: Terminal state and output digest
pairs.detail: What actually shipped and under which retry lineage.

variants.hint: A seed by itself is not a replay contract.
variants.explanation: The manifest exists so a result can be explained or replayed, which needs identity, versions, sampling contract, timings, and outcome together.
